surface_form_payload.question_text: Assign the frequency, severity, and qualitative risk categories independently.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Design intent (inferred from the listed causes): keep the V-001 liquid level within its control band by discharging liquid through LV-101/LV-102 and SDV-101/SDV-102. Deviation Level/More: each listed cause restricts liquid outflow while inflow continues. Frequency C (Casual): four separate, common valve or control-loop failure modes make high level credible several times over plant life. However, escalation to flooding and carryover requires both high-level functions (LAH-102 and LAHH-103, each closing inlet SDV-30010) to fail. Severity III (Average): the worst listed consequences are asset and operational (flooding, liquid carryover to the gas line and treatment unit, possible generator damage, shutdown, production loss). No injury, fire or loss of containment is stated. Matrix III/C gives M. Sensitivity: III with B to D, or II with C to D, all remain M. H would require IV with D, or III with E, which the packet does not support. Shutdown and production loss also follow successful SDV-30010 action, so the safeguards do not prevent them. Recommendations: confirm LAH-102 and LAHH-103 are independent of the LV-101/LV-102 control measurements; verify SDV-30010 closure time against the level-rise time from LAHH to flooding; evaluate a diverse final element and/or liquid protection upstream of the generators; review the spurious-trip reliability of SDV-101/SDV-102. Subjective probability (judgment aid only, not a quantitative risk estimate): about 15% that a high-level event escalates to actual flooding or liquid carryover at least once over a nominal operating life, with existing safeguards credited.
safeguards_considered: LAHH-103 high-high level function closing SDV-30010 (inlet isolation): the main automatic barrier against overfill and carryover. Its SIL, proof testing and response time are not stated.

LAH-102 high level function with SDV-30010 closing action: gives early warning and a second closure demand. It shares the final element SDV-30010 with LAHH-103 and may share measurement with the LV-102 control loop, so it is not credited as fully independent.
The packet lists no downstream liquid knock-out, scrubber or generator fuel-gas liquid protection, so none is credited.
The existing safeguards mitigate flooding and carryover but not unit shutdown or production loss, which result from SDV-30010 closure itself.

supporting_evidence.relevance: Defines the node scope: V-001 and associated lines.
The Level/More guideword pairing sets the deviation under study.
The deviation is more liquid in V-001 (high level), leading toward flooding.
Four separate outlet-restriction causes (spurious SDV-101/SDV-102 closure, LV-101/LV-102 failure) are common failure modes and support a credible, recurring initiating frequency.

The consequences are asset and operational (flooding, carryover to gas line and treatment unit, possible generator damage, shutdown, production loss), with no injury or release stated. This is the basis for severity III.
Two high-level functions both close SDV-30010, reducing the likelihood of escalation (basis for frequency C). They share one final element, which limits independent credit.

uncertainty_notes: The packet gives no numeric definitions for the frequency categories and no failure-rate or operating-history data, so frequency C is a qualitative judgment.

The packet does not say whether frequency is rated before or after crediting safeguards. The unmitigated high-level deviation from four common valve or control-loop failures could reasonably be rated D, which still maps to M at severity III.

Severity depends on the extent of the 'possible damage to the unit generators'. If generator damage were major, or caused loss of essential power with safety implications, severity IV would be arguable, and IV with frequency D maps to H.

The packet does not state whether LAH-102 (and possibly LAHH-103) is independent of the LV-101/LV-102 level-control measurements. Both safeguards act on the same final element, SDV-30010, so their combined credit is limited by this common-mode dependency.

The packet gives no information on vessel configuration, surge time between LAH, LAHH and flooding, SDV-30010 closure time, SIL or proof testing, or any downstream scrubber or knock-out protecting the gas treatment unit and generators.
The wording 'closed-circuit failure' for LV-101/LV-102 is ambiguous (fail-closed valve vs. control-loop failure). It is interpreted here as any failure that restricts liquid outflow.
The subjective probability is a judgment aid only. It is not derived from packet data, assumes a nominal multi-decade operating life, and is not a quantitative risk estimate.
